model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Proposed one portable SWAR block-validation experiment with explicit cross-block and tail state; kept the scalar validator for comparison and tail handling.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: The candidate uses standard integer operations rather than target-specific SIMD instructions, so it does not depend on unverified hardware or compiler capabilities.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: No ISA-specific intrinsic, API, compiler option, or hardware property is assumed by this portable SWAR experiment.

model_reported.summary: Reported the measured valid baseline only and left speed and correctness of this candidate to the controller; no candidate improvement is asserted.

proposal.hypothesis: Portable 8-byte SWAR masks may reduce per-byte control flow on mixed-width inputs by classifying byte lanes, shifting lead masks into expected continuation positions, checking restricted second-byte ranges, and carrying boundary state. The lane-mask and carry bookkeeping may instead cost more than the scalar control, so this is a hypothesis to measure, not a claimed speedup.

retained: Retained the supplied scalar validator as validate_utf8_scalar for the scalar control and tail validation.
Added portable 64-bit byte-lane bit-plane extraction and classification for eight-byte blocks.
Built shifted continuation masks and checked UTF-8 starter validity, including C0/C1 and F5-F7 exclusions.
Checked E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte restrictions within and across block boundaries.
Carried up to three pending continuation bytes into the next block and validated a bounded scalar tail without overreading.

proposal.hypothesis: A safer hybrid may retain the throughput benefit of portable 8-byte bit-mask validation for complete blocks while avoiding fragile carried boundary state: when a block may end inside a code point, validate that block and the remaining suffix with the supplied scalar control. This tests whole-block classification and constraint masks while preserving scalar handling for boundary cases.

retained: Preserved the supplied scalar UTF-8 validator as a correctness control and suffix fallback.
Used portable 64-bit word classification to validate fully contained 8-byte blocks, including continuation placement and restricted second-byte constraints.
When valid prefix masks indicate a sequence may cross a block boundary, delegated validation from that block through the end to the scalar control instead of carrying pending/range state.
Retained a scalar bounded-tail path for remaining bytes.
